prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched parameters via naive substring/regex search, which could false-positive on commas or parameter-name substrings inside quoted values. Both replace it with a hand-rolled tokenizer that walks the header character-by-character, tracking quote state and backslash escapes, to split on only top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched parameters via naive substring/regex search, which could false-positive on commas or parameter-name substrings inside quoted values. Both replace it with a hand-rolled tokenizer that walks the header character-by-character, tracking quote state and backslash escapes, to split on only top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header value (not just the portion after the first space) and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme/remainder to detect where a new auth-scheme challenge begins. This means it can correctly handle a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer realm="a", Basic realm="b"') by stopping collection at the next scheme token. 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space (assumed to be the single leading scheme name) and then treats every remaining top-level-comma-separated token as a Bearer param, so a second scheme in the same header would be mis-parsed as an extra parameter rather than recognized as a new challenge.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header value (not just the portion after the first space) and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme/remainder to detect where a new auth-scheme challenge begins. This means it can correctly handle a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer realm="a", Basic realm="b"') by stopping collection at the next scheme token. 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space (assumed to be the single leading scheme name) and then treats every remaining top-level-comma-separated token as a Bearer param, so a second scheme in the same header would be mis-parsed as an extra parameter rather than recognized as a new challenge.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header value (not just the portion after the first space) and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly partitions each comma-separated segment into scheme/remainder to detect where a new auth-scheme challenge begins. This means it can correctly handle a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer realm="a", Basic realm="b"') by stopping collection at the next scheme token. 3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space (assumed to be the single leading scheme name) and then treats every remaining top-level-comma-separated token as a Bearer param, so a second scheme in the same header would be mis-parsed as an extra parameter rather than recognized as a new challenge.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously matched parameters via naive substring/regex search, which could false-positive on commas or parameter-name substrings inside quoted values. Both replace it with a hand-rolled tokenizer that walks the header character-by-character, tracking quote state and backslash escapes, to split on only top-level (unquoted) commas.
